title: Tries and Text-Based Data Structures
description: Explore Tries, their structure, and applications in text-based problems like autocomplete and spell-checking.

quiz.question: What is a Trie data structure primarily used for?
options: Efficient string retrieval and prefix-based searching
quiz.correctAnswer: Efficient string retrieval and prefix-based searching
quiz.explanation: Tries are designed to store strings and facilitate fast prefix-based lookups.

quiz.question: In a Trie, what does each node typically represent?
options: A pointer to a child node only
quiz.explanation: Each node represents a character in the string stored in the Trie.

quiz.question: What is the time complexity to search for a word in a Trie of length n?
quiz.explanation: Searching in a Trie depends on the length of the word, so it is O(n).

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of using Tries?
quiz.explanation: Tries can consume large memory, especially with large alphabets or sparse data.

quiz.question: What kind of problem is best solved by a Trie?
options: Finding all words starting with a given prefix
Finding the shortest path in a graph
quiz.correctAnswer: Finding all words starting with a given prefix
quiz.explanation: Tries excel at prefix-based queries like autocomplete.

quiz.question: Which of the following is a common use case for Tries?
quiz.explanation: Tries enable fast retrieval of words matching a prefix, useful for autocomplete.

quiz.question: In a Trie, how do you mark the end of a word?
options: By a special boolean flag in the node
By storing the length of the word
quiz.correctAnswer: By a special boolean flag in the node
quiz.explanation: Nodes have a flag to indicate if they represent the end of a valid word.

quiz.question: Which of the following is a drawback of Tries?
options: High memory usage for large alphabets
quiz.correctAnswer: High memory usage for large alphabets
quiz.explanation: Tries can be memory-intensive when the alphabet size is large.

quiz.question: What is the space complexity of a Trie storing k words of average length n?
quiz.explanation: In the worst case, each character can occupy a node, leading to O(k*n) space.

quiz.question: Besides Tries, which data structure is often used for efficient string matching?
quiz.explanation: Suffix trees are advanced data structures used for string pattern matching.
